blocks.x: A working definition of Insurance & Risk for Insurance & Risk: engineered controls, named owners, weekly evidence, and a signed baseline so every claim of improvement can be replayed line by line.

Insurance is a decision business wrapped in a promise: price the risk correctly, honor the claim quickly, hold the reserves honestly. All three now depend on machinery most carriers have underinvested in — pricing models that see the portfolio's drift, claims pipelines that read documents instead of waiting for humans, and reserving analytics that reconcile actuarial judgment with live experience data.

blocks.note: What the diagram shows: decisions as first-class records — the decision, its evidence and its owner bound together from creation.

blocks.x: The industry's structural pressures compound: catastrophe volatility reprices property books annually, combined-ratio pressure meets softening cycles, and fraud has industrialized on both sides of the ledger. Meanwhile distribution shifts — embedded insurance, ecosystems, digital MGAs — reward carriers whose underwriting and claims engines can plug into partners' platforms through APIs rather than PDFs.
